general.title: How to listen
paragraphs: The app already level-matches and time-aligns A and B. You are listening for codec damage, not loudness or delay. Use headphones; open-backs in the Sundara class make air and cymbals easier, but any honest pair is fine.

Start at 32 or 64 kbps MP3 if you have not done this before — the damage is obvious. Then step to 96 kbps. That is the interesting test. 128 kbps is often subtle; treat a “maybe” as a maybe and switch to Blind ABX.

Loop a short region (5–15 seconds) and flip A/B on the same playhead. Long unbroken listens cause fatigue and false confidence. If your ears feel dull, stop. The clock on the player is MM:SS — seek to the cue, then loop by ear with ← →.

generic.title: Imported file
generic.stresses: Whatever is sharp, noisy, or very quiet in your recording — attacks, cymbals, applause, reverb tails, or hiss.
generic.lossyDoes: At 64–128 kbps, attacks soften or grow a pre-echo smear, air goes dull or fizzy, and a quiet noise floor can warble.

listenWhere.note: Pick a 8–12 s loop with transients or audible air. Skip long held notes with nothing around them.

generic.howToUse: Same as bundled clips: short A/B loops, headphones, start obvious (64 kbps) then try 96.

goldberg-aria.title: Bach — Goldberg Aria
goldberg-aria.stresses: Isolated piano hammers and the quiet harmonic decay after each note. Almost no drums or mix to hide damage.
goldberg-aria.lossyDoes: Hammers lose a bit of click; the sustain can turn grainy or “swishy,” and the space between notes fills with a faint warble.

listenWhere.note: First notes: clean attacks and long tails. High relative 96 kbps residual on this opening.
Louder phrase; one of the two largest mid-clip residuals versus 96 kbps MP3.
Same kind of writing later in the Aria — the other mid-clip residual peak.

goldberg-aria.howToUse: Loop one 8 s phrase. A/B on a single hammer, then sit on the decay. If 96 kbps feels identical, you are not failing — solo piano often is close at that rate.

goldberg-variatio-1.title: Bach — Goldberg Variatio 1
goldberg-variatio-1.stresses: Faster two-part piano writing: many closely spaced attacks and crossing lines.
goldberg-variatio-1.lossyDoes: Pre-echo smear just before notes, inner-voice muddle, and a slightly softer top on the loudest peaks.

listenWhere.note: Early figuration — highest relative 96 kbps residual in the first half.
Busiest stretch (also among the loudest). Largest absolute residual versus 96 kbps MP3.

goldberg-variatio-1.howToUse: Loop 1:16–1:24 and ask whether both hands stay distinct. Then try the calmer 0:10 passage to hear smear without the extra level.

beethoven-op18-6-i.title: Beethoven — Quartet Op. 18/6, I
beethoven-op18-6-i.stresses: Bow noise, ensemble attacks, and inner voices that sit under the first violin.
beethoven-op18-6-i.lossyDoes: Rosiny air on the bows dulls; tutti chords smear; quiet inner lines can go watery.

listenWhere.note: First dense tutti — loudest 8 s in the clip and a top absolute residual versus 96 kbps MP3.
Later high-energy passage. Highest relative residual in the movement; more bow/air than the opening.

beethoven-op18-6-i.howToUse: Loop a tutti, then a bar or two after it when the texture thins. Listen for the viola/second violin, not just the tune.

njhb-checking-for-traps.title: NJHB — Checking For Traps
njhb-checking-for-traps.stresses: Cymbals and brushes, trumpet attacks, vibes, and a full combo competing for bits.
njhb-checking-for-traps.lossyDoes: Cymbal air turns fizzy or dull, trumpet fronts soften, and the ride pattern blurs into the mix.

listenWhere.note: Opening has the most high-frequency energy in the excerpt (cymbal/brush air).
Loudest combo stretch and a top absolute 96 kbps residual.
Another high-residual chorus — good second loop if the intro feels too thin.

njhb-checking-for-traps.howToUse: Loop the intro and listen only to the metal. Then jump to 0:24 and A/B the trumpet front. 96 kbps is the useful step after 64 sounds easy.

jahzzar-missing-you.title: Jahzzar — Missing You
jahzzar-missing-you.stresses: Synth/noise air and a dense layered pop mix. This is the default “easy to hear” track for a reason.
jahzzar-missing-you.lossyDoes: The airy bed warbles or goes dull; the chorus congests; hi-hat/noise texture is the first thing to collapse.

listenWhere.note: Standout cue: very high >8 kHz energy and the highest relative 96 kbps residual in the song (the codec eats the air).
Loudest full-mix chorus — largest absolute residual. Good for congestion rather than hush.

jahzzar-missing-you.howToUse: The setup default (32 kbps MP3) should be obvious. Then loop 0:36–0:50 at 96 kbps. If you can still hear the air change, try Blind ABX.

applause-large-hall.title: Applause — Large hall
applause-large-hall.stresses: Dense unpitched clap transients plus a reverberant noise floor. Built as a codec-stress texture, not a song.
applause-large-hall.lossyDoes: Claps smear into a swish, the hall noise warbles or “breathes,” and the stereo image can collapse. Pre-echo is common.

listenWhere.note: Densest continuous clapping — highest absolute 96 kbps residual.
Texture thins; relative error goes up and the high band stays busy. Easier to hear the noise floor warble.

applause-large-hall.howToUse: Loop 0:03–0:13. This one is often obvious at 96 kbps. If it is, step to 128 and see when the swish disappears.

guitar-satie-gymnopedie-1.title: Satie — Gymnopédie No. 1
guitar-satie-gymnopedie-1.stresses: Fingerstyle pluck attacks, nail/string buzz, and a long quiet decay with room air.
guitar-satie-gymnopedie-1.lossyDoes: Plucks lose their click, decays go grainy, and the faint buzz/air after the note disappears.

listenWhere.note: Opening arpeggio — brightest high-frequency content in the performance.
Another high-residual phrase if you want a mid-piece loop.
Louder closing phrases — largest absolute 96 kbps residual.

guitar-satie-gymnopedie-1.howToUse: Loop the first 16 s. A/B on one pluck, then let the decay run. Soft guitar is easy to miss at 96 kbps; give the tail time.

transients.title: Transients
transients.stresses: Isolated clicks with silence between them. Designed to show pre-echo.
transients.lossyDoes: A faint whoosh or double-hit appears before the click, and the click itself gets fatter.

listenWhere.note: Clicks are placed at about 0:00.4, 0:01.1, 0:01.8, 0:02.9, and so on through 0:22.7.
Largest 96 kbps residual window. Brightest individual clicks near 0:07 and 0:18.

transients.howToUse: Loop 0:14–0:22 and listen *before* each click. If you only hear the hit, you are listening too late.

harmonics.title: Harmonic study
harmonics.stresses: Stacked harmonic tones and their decay — especially the higher notes.
harmonics.lossyDoes: Upper harmonics dull; decays warble or lose pitch focus.

listenWhere.note: High stacked note (around 0:14.6) is the largest 96 kbps residual. The next tone at 0:16 sits in the same window.
24 s total. Any sustain after an attack is fair game if the high note feels too brief.

harmonics.howToUse: Loop 0:14–0:20 and listen to the top of the chord, not the fundamental. Short loop, a few A/B flips, then stop.

dense-mix.title: Dense mix
dense-mix.stresses: Pad, kick, hats, and a little noise at once — masking versus exposed cymbal ticks.
dense-mix.lossyDoes: Hats lose fizz, pad edges smear, and the kick stays while the top end dulls.

listenWhere.note: The texture is continuous for 24 s. Residual versus 96 kbps MP3 is fairly even.
Hats/noise are more exposed against a quieter pad (higher relative residual). 0:15–0:23 is a similar stretch.

dense-mix.howToUse: Loop either 8 s region and lock onto the hat tick. Ignore the kick; it usually survives.
